beliefs: On x>=0, f(x) = 106.06 + 111.43*x is accurate to ~0.1% across 0 to 127, including x=0 [E1, E2, E3, E12]
On x<=-2, f(x) = 26.07*|x| - 25.4 is accurate to ~0.1% across |x| from 2 to 128 [E5, E6, E3, E4, E14]
The negative branch has a smooth minimum near |x|=1.07 with f≈6.37 [E7, E9, E10, E13, E20, E21]
Between |x|=1.07 and |x|=2 the trough rises smoothly and joins the linear law at |x|=2 (f(-1.5)=13.66, f(-1.8)=21.48, f(-1.98)=26.18) [E13, E14, E15, E20, E22]
The trough between |x|=1.07 and 2 is very close to a parabola in |x| but with slight residual curvature; a cubic through dense points fits better than a pure quadratic [E13, E20, E22, E23]?
The near-zero negative fall between |x|=0 and 1 is a smooth curve; a quartic through dense observed points captures it to ~1% [E16, E17, E18, E19, E21]
notes: E23 shows the trough is not exactly a parabola (residual curvature ~0.2-0.5). Replaced the quadratic trough with a cubic fit through dense observed points from |x|=1.07 to 2.0, and kept the quartic for the near-zero fall. Also fixed the join at |x|=2 to match f(-2)=26.6982.
